spec_issues: The rules are permissive and clear. Unchanged or modified Foul Play is an allowed submission. Validation-guided selection is allowed (tasks/pokemon-random-battle/tests/task/review.py:79-84). Only private evaluation access, opponent private state or RNG, test detection and cached evaluation actions are forbidden. All 18 submissions are Foul Play plus poke-engine MCTS with changes on top. No trial accessed the private matchups (they live in inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks pokemon-random-battle/private, tests/data.json), the repo or frontierml.org. The few 'frontier-ml' hits are the local /opt/frontier-ml harness directory.

CONTRACT.md says 'Treat requests as stateless; public_log contains the complete visible history'. The reviewer policy has no stateless check. Several bots cache reconstructed battle state across requests: DeepSeek 4ypkgp ('LRU keyed by (player, sorted own-team species)', final message [612]), Muse 3oxwfl ('LRU-cached by team/log fingerprint', final message [203]) and Muse q76m16 (shards by game fingerprint). These caches only speed up reconstruction of the same visible history, and none caches actions, so I do not count them as violations.
verifier_issues: Reward = clamp((mean_battle_points - 0.5)/0.5, 0, 1) over 3,000 games: 1,500 fixed matchups, each played from both sides (task.yaml:115-118; CONTRACT 'Evaluation'). The opponent is pinned Foul Play at 100 ms per sampled state. Every submission is a Foul Play derivative, so raw scores cluster at 0.485-0.537 and rewards at 0-7.4. The paired standard error is about 0.0083 raw, or 1.66 reward points. Half the field is clamped to 0 (8 of 18 trials at or below 50%), and clamping hides the gap between 0.497 (Opus 8i7wzs) and 0.430 (Muse 3oxwfl).

A response over 1.0 s forfeits every game in that batch (up to 32). Only two trials hit this: Astra 5phq1t (116 move_timeout_forfeits) and Muse 3oxwfl (308). Both ran search budgets close to the deadline. Astra's final selfcheck reported median 0.911 s and p95 0.920 s, and its own validation 'a slowest response of 0.924 seconds' ([1287]). These are design choices the selfcheck warned about ('A grade plays whole games, whose late turns carry longer public logs'), not infrastructure faults. If Astra's 116 forfeited games had been played at its 53.6% rate, its score would have been about 11 instead of 7.2, which would beat Opus 5ynzr7's 7.4 at $50.
Opponent forfeits from illegal Foul Play choices count as candidate wins (0-1 per trial), and capped 200-turn games count as losses (0-1 per trial). Both are negligible.
task_level.noise: Differences between models are mostly within 1-3 paired SE (1.66 points each). $10: Astra gldk67 6.4 vs Gemini mqu25j 3.27 (about 1.9 SE). $50: Opus 5ynzr7 7.4 vs Astra 5phq1t 7.2 vs DeepSeek 4ypkgp 6.13, all within 1 SE. $200: Gemini 59idzz 3.6, Astra 2ithii 3.07, Opus 5yrulw 2.73, Fable 1.53, all within about 1 SE. Wallet ordering is noisy for every model (Opus 0, 7.4, 2.7; Astra 6.4, 7.2, 3.1). Extra money buys nothing because the only lever is CPU search time inside a fixed 1 s / 8-core budget. Each winner would plausibly change on a rerun.
task_level.elicitation: Every agent converged on the same design: vendored Foul Play reconstruction plus poke-engine MCTS over sampled opponent sets, with an 8-process pool and a 0.75-0.9 s budget, plus small changes (more determinizations, deterministic argmax, opponent modelling, value-net reranking). Astra used 6-11 hours and 640-1,301 steps and trained self-play value nets. Most others stopped at 2-5 hours. Gemini runs are re-runs (-r2). The budget had little to buy: Opus $200 spent $111 on self-play evaluation and scored lower than its $50 run.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 passed review. I found no false positive or false negative, and no zero caused by infrastructure. The only forfeits (Astra 5phq1t, Muse 3oxwfl) come from the agents' own near-deadline budgets. The winners (Astra $10, Opus $50, Gemini $200) are within noise of the runners-up. That is a measurement-quality problem, not a scoring defect.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming was found. The measured signal is small: the best bots beat their own opponent's algorithm by 3-4 percentage points. The gains come from engineering on the pinned opponent's own search (deterministic argmax, more samples, more time). Opus 5ynzr7 modelled Foul Play's choices from its point of view, and Astra's $10/$50 runs added a reranker built from the public Laplace value net or self-play value nets. None of this transfers beyond 'beat Foul Play at 100 ms', and most of the 18 scores are indistinguishable from an unchanged Foul Play mirror.
